subject: CoreFin - regional failover RTO/RPO exception request
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@corefin.com>

Cc: CoreFin Procurement <procurement@corefin.com>, CoreFin Legal <legal@corefin.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 11:23:00 AM PDT
Subject: Request: regional failover RTO/RPO exception for COREFIN contract

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we finalize the SOW and SLA language for CoreFin's production cutover, procurement & legal asked me to surface one request up front so we can get it into the redline process rather than iterating later.

Summary: CoreFin is asking for a temporary exception to the standard cross-region failover RTO for our first 12 months of live traffic. We have strict reconciliation and settlement windows that make immediate failover risky for downstream systems, and our payments ledger sync is periodically run in a controlled window. Specifically we are requesting:

- A documented exception allowing up to 8 hours RTO for a multi-region failover (active -> warm-standby) for the first 12 months, with defined mitigations and a joint runbook.
- A defined RPO tolerance (up to 30 minutes for ledger writes during failover) limited to the services listed in the attached spreadsheet.
- A liability carveout/limitation language for cross-region failover events tied to this agreed exception.

Attached: corefin_exception_request.pdf (formal request), prod-traffic-snapshot.csv (monthly peak windows).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a scoped, documented exception, and if so what we would need (playbook, telemetry, acceptance tests, cost uplift)? Procurement needs a plan and timeline by Friday so legal can draft initial redlines.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 30-min call to go through specifics.

Best,
Emily Chen
Director, Infrastructure Programs
CoreFin Payments

--

Short answer: we can scope a documented exception with defined mitigations, but there are trade-offs (operational complexity, observability commitments, and a modest one-time onboarding uplift). I’ve looped Stephanie (our reliability lead) to define the technical boundary and acceptance criteria, and Aditya (sales lead) to help surface commercial terms.

Proposed next steps:
1) Stephanie drafts a scoped playbook and a short tech appendix listing which services can be in the 8-hour window vs which must remain under the standard 1-hour RTO.
2) We capture required telemetry and acceptance tests (synthetic failover drills + 7-day post-cutover monitoring).
3) We propose a one-time implementation uplift (engineering hours) and a temporary premium on Dedicated capacity during the first 12 months.
4) We provide a draft MAP and redline language for legal to start with by Friday as requested.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call this afternoon (2pm PT) or tomorrow morning? If not, we’ll proceed over email and aim to send the draft playbook by EOD Thursday.

Hi Emily — appreciate the detail. I reviewed the snapshot and the requested scope and put together an initial technical position. High-level points below; I’ll attach a short diff of the playbook (link in related_links).

Technical position (initial):
- Scope: We can agree to a scoped 8-hour RTO for cross-region recovery for a defined subset of CoreFin services (settlements, batch reconciliation pipelines). Critical front-end & customer-facing paths (API gateway, tokenization, user sessions) must remain under the standard 1-hour RTO — we cannot put transactional ingress into an 8-hour window.
- RPO: 30-minute RPO is achievable for the ledger write flows if we enable nearline replication (async with strong acknowledgement). That will require additional storage/replication throughput and will increase cost. Full KV cache state cannot be guaranteed; we recommend graceful degradation of caches and stateless fallback paths.
- Acceptance criteria: (a) two successful staged failover rehearsals with synthetic traffic simulating peak windows, (b) monitoring hooks for token-level latency and reconciliation drift, (c) a signed runbook with rollback criteria.
- Operational mitigations: manual gating for full switch-over (human-in-the-loop for final switchover during the first 90 days), extended post-failover monitoring window (72 hours), and a joint incident bridge policy.
- Cost/effort: estimate ~5-7 engineer-weeks to implement nearline replication, orchestration for staged failovers, and the additional observability. We can provide a fixed SOW for this work or include it as a time-and-materials uplift on top of Dedicated capacity.

If CoreFin accepts the constrained scope above, we will:
1) Produce the playbook diff and annotated runbook by EOD Thursday (link to drive provided).
2) Provide a test plan for the two staged rehearsals and proposed windows (non-peak + one peak).
3) Deliver suggested redline language for the SLA section covering the temporary exception, the rollback provisions, and the liability carveout.

If you want, I’m available for the 2pm PT call to walk through the items and answer security-related questions.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emily — quick follow to confirm alignment and next steps.

Summary of what Redwood will deliver for the MAP / contract redline:
- Scoped exception limited to the services listed in prod-traffic-snapshot.csv with an explicit list embedded in the SLA appendix.
- Temporary RTO of up to 8 hours for those scoped services for 12 months, with a 30-minute RPO for ledger flows where nearline replication is enabled.
- Operational requirements: two successful staged rehearsals (non-peak + peak), signed runbook, human-in-the-loop gating for initial switchover, and extended 72-hour monitoring window.
- Commercials: a one-time implementation uplift (SOW) plus a temporary premium for Dedicated capacity during the 12-month exception period.
- Liability language: Redwood will propose a narrowly-scoped limitation tied exclusively to the agreed exception events; legal teams can exchange redlines against the draft we will send.
